**San Marino** (/ˌsæn məˈriːnoʊ/ ⓘ *SAN mə-REE-noh*, Template:IPA-it; Template:Lang-rgn or *San Maroin*), officially the **Republic of San Marino**[1][2][8] (Template:Lang-it) and also known as the **Most Serene Republic of San Marino**[9] (Template:Lang-it), is a European microstate and country enclaved by Italy.[10] Located on the northeastern side of the Apennine Mountains, San Marino is the fifth-smallest country in the world[11] and covers a land area of just over 61 km2 (23+1⁄2 sq mi), with a population of 33,660 as of 2022.[4]


San Marino is a landlocked country; however, its northeastern end is within ten kilometres (six miles) of the Italian city of Rimini on the Adriatic coast. The nearest airport is also in Italy. The country's capital city, the City of San Marino, is located atop Monte Titano, while its largest settlement is Dogana within the largest municipality of Serravalle. San Marino's official language is Italian.

**Liechtenstein** (/ˈlɪktənstaɪn/;[11] Template:IPA-de), officially the **Principality of Liechtenstein** (Template:Lang-de, pronounced [ˈfʏʁstn̩tuːm ˈlɪçtn̩ˌʃtaɪ̯n] ⓘ),[12] is a German-speaking and doubly landlocked country and microstate located in the Alps between Austria and Switzerland.[13] It is the sixth smallest nation worldwide.[14]
Liechtenstein is a semi-constitutional monarchy headed by the prince of Liechtenstein.


Liechtenstein is bordered by Switzerland to the west and south and Austria to the east and north. It is Europe's fourth-smallest country, with an area of just over 160 square kilometres (62 square miles) and a population of 38,749 (as of 2019[update]).[15] Divided into 11 municipalities, its capital is Vaduz, and its largest municipality is Schaan. It is also the smallest country to border two countries.[16]

<title>Andorra</title>
<fragment>

Andorra is the sixth-smallest state in Europe, with an area of 468 square kilometres (181 sq mi) and a population of approximately 79,034.[15][16] The Andorran people are a Romance ethnic group closely related to Catalans.[17] Andorra is the world's 16th-smallest country by land and 11th-smallest by population.[18] Its capital, Andorra la Vella, is the highest capital city in Europe, at an elevation of 1,023 metres (3,356 feet) above sea level.[19] The official language is Catalan, but Spanish, Occitan, and French are also commonly spoken.[3][20]


Tourism in Andorra brings an estimated 10.2 million visitors to the country annually.[21] Andorra is not a member state of the European Union. It has been a member of the United Nations since 1993.[22]

English is less commonly spoken among the general population, though it is understood to varying degrees in the major tourist resorts.[*citation needed*] Andorra is one of only four European countries (together with France, Monaco, and Turkey)[183] that have never signed the Council of Europe Framework Convention on National Minorities.[184]

## 1. 摩纳哥 (Monaco)
- **地理位置**：位于法国东南部地中海沿岸
- **特点**：世界第二小的国家，以豪华赌场、Formula 1大奖赛和富裕居民著称
- **官方语言**：法语

## 2. 梵蒂冈 (Vatican City)  
- **地理位置**：意大利罗马城内的国中之国
- **特点**：世界最小的国家，天主教会的中心，拥有西斯廷教堂和圣彼得大教堂
- **官方语言**：意大利语、拉丁语

## 3. 圣马力诺 (San Marino)
- **面积**：61.2平方公里
- **人口**：约33,660人 (2022年)
- **地理位置**：完全被意大利包围的内陆国家
- **特点**：世界第五小国家，位于亚平宁山脉东北侧
- **官方语言**：意大利语
- **货币**：欧元

## 4. 列支敦士登 (Liechtenstein)
- **面积**：约160平方公里  
- **人口**：约38,749人 (2019年)
- **地理位置**：位于奥地利和瑞士之间的阿尔卑斯山区
- **特点**：世界第六小国家，唯一同时与奥地利和瑞士接壤的国家
- **官方语言**：德语
- **货币**：瑞士法郎

## 5. 马耳他 (Malta)
- **地理位置**：地中海中部的岛国
- **特点**：位于意大利西西里岛以南80公里处
- **官方语言**：马耳他语、英语
- **欧盟成员国**

## 6. 安道尔 (Andorra)
- **面积**：468平方公里
- **人口**：约79,034人
- **地理位置**：位于法国和西班牙之间的比利牛斯山脉
- **特点**：欧洲第六小国家，首都安道尔城是欧洲海拔最高的首都(1,023米)
- **官方语言**：加泰罗尼亚语
- **经济**：以旅游业为主，年接待游客约1,020万

这些微型国家各具特色，从梵蒂冈的宗教影响力到摩纳哥的奢华生活，从圣马力诺的历史传承到列支敦士登的金融中心地位，都展现了欧洲多样性的独特魅力。
